A very warm welcome to Shipton Bellinger Primary School
Here at Shipton Bellinger Primary School, our core purpose is to provide a safe and respectful learning environment where everyone can grow and achieve together. We are a small village primary school located in the heart of a military community, close to Tidworth, the historical town of Salisbury and Stonehenge . If this is your first visit to our website we trust it gives you a flavour of what we offer.
If you would like more information or would like to arrange an appointment to visit in person please feel free to give the school office a call, they will be very happy to help you.
Latest News
The disco was a great success with lots of amazing costumes. The children demonstrated their dance moves and getting some spooky stencils too! The dice game was once again a big hit and the usual favourites ‘Cha cha slide’ and the ‘Macarena’ brought everyone to the dance floor!
On Thursday morning all the children took part in our annual Harvest Festival service at St. Peters Church. Thank you to Mrs Webber for organising the event and all the staff for their class preparations. We enjoyed learning about Autumn, Harvest Traditions and Harvest around the wrodl. Thank you for all the donations for Andover Foodbank too. These have been greatly received.
We had the privilege on Wednesday afternoon to have members of our Fijian community come into school and proudly shared their traditions and facts about their country. All the children in the school joined in and waved their Fijian flags. It was a lovely experience for the whole school to be part of. Thank you to Mrs Fotofili for organising it and to the rest of our Fijian community for involving us in their special day.

Our STAR Learning Values
At Shipton Bellinger primary School our core purpose is to provide a safe and respectful learning environment where everyone can grow and achieve together.
Get in Touch

Welcome to Shipton Bellinger Primary School
A very warm welcome to Shipton Bellinger Primary School.
We are a small village primary school located in the heart of a military community.
Located close to Tidworth, the historical town of Salisbury and Stonehenge; coupled with our extensive school grounds, we have a vast selection of amenities on our doorstep to inspire our curriculum. We encourage our children to explore, take risks and learn from experiences on offer; building strong foundations for a life-long love of learning and allowing our children to develop their natural talents.
Our dedicated and talented staff nurture children as individuals and it is our positive relationships with pupils and parents that makes us who we are - an achieving, smiling, family school.
If this is your first visit to our website we trust it gives you a flavour of what we offer. If you would like more information or would like to arrange an appointment to visit in person please feel free to give the school office a call, they will be very happy to help you.
Groups of children often explore the village environment as part of their topic work and local visitors share their knowledge of the locality. Several of our neighbours help in the school with gardening, worship and baking. We welcome a wide range of visitors.
We have strong links with the services, including having been adopted by the Local REME BN who help us with hands-on projects in the school and grounds. Head over to our Service Families page to explore this partnership further.
Junior children swim at Tidworth Leisure Centre and we belong to the Rural Schools Group where we have links with schools at Kimpton, Appleshaw, Amport, Grateley and Abbots Ann. The Year 6 teacher liaises with John Hanson and Wellington and other secondary schools, and pupils enjoy an induction day prior to their transfer.
We invite outside agencies to work with our children and have links with Andover Rugby Club for tag rugby, Andover Cricket Club and the Mountbatten Sports Partnership. We have a School Sports Co-ordinator who organises events for children both in school and in the wider community.
Get in Touch

Modern Foreign Languages (MFL) - French
A high-quality languages education should foster pupils’ curiosity and deepen their understanding of the world. Teaching should enable pupils to express their ideas in another language and to communicate for practical purposes. Our Key Stage 2 classes learn French as their modern foreign language. Key Stage One classes are exposed to the French language through songs and nursery rhymes.
We use the Language Angels program of study to ensure that our curriculum is sequential, systematic and engaging. The Language Angels curriculum is carefully planned around logical progression in phonics, vocabulary and grammar.
Ongoing assessment throughout the units of learning ensures that the language being taught is carefully planned and tailored to build on pupils’ ability and prior knowledge.
Get in Touch

Music
"Music is the universal language of mankind." - Henry Wadsworth Longfellow
“There is no feeling, except the extremes of fear and grief that does not find relief in music.” - George Eliot
“Music acts like a magic key, to which the most tightly closed heart opens.” - Maria von Trapp
“Can a mere song change people's minds? I doubt that it is so. But a song can infiltrate your heart and the heart may change your mind.” - Elvis Costello
Here at Shipton Bellinger, we strive to ensure learners will celebrate a range of musical genres and song during weekly singing assemblies. Threaded throughout our assembly musical programme with inspirational musicians in mind, the children are exposed to a range of composers and musicians across the eras. From these weekly assemblies, pupils are able to apply their learning through preparing for performances in the Church to celebrate key events within our community such as Easter.
We are also the home of the 'Shipton Singers' extra-curricular club, a collection of talented singers who attend every week to celebrate music from different countries to incorporate our diverse world as well as being taught how to sing and use their voice in different ways with Mrs. Lane. Outside of school, there are a range of opportunities for extra-curricular instrument lessons including piano and guitar.
Get in Touch

Well-Being & Mental Health Resources
Families thrive when they feel understood, supported, and connected. This section brings together guidance, practical tools, and trusted information to help parents and carers navigate the emotional ups and downs of family life. Whether you’re looking for strategies to support your child, ways to strengthen your own wellbeing, or simply reassurance that you’re not alone, this space is designed to offer calm, clarity, and confidence. It’s a place where families can find support that is compassionate, accessible, and grounded in what really makes a difference.
We work closely with parents and carers to promote positive mental health. Our approach includes:
If you are worried about your child’s wellbeing, please speak to your child’s class teacher or contact our Designated Safeguarding Lead. We are here to help.
Further Guidance for Parents and Families
Below is a curated set of guidance, practical tools, and trusted information drawn directly from reputable UK organisations that specialise in supporting parents, carers, and families with mental health and wellbeing. Each item includes a brief explanation so you can quickly see what it offers.

Mind – Parenting and Mental Health

Art
At Shipton Bellinger we empower our learners to become artists who create, craft and express their individuality in a variety of creative ways.
We explore key artists and a diverse and exciting range of cultures, media and artistic styles. Using these carefully chosen artists as inspiration, we develop the skills and knowledge necessary to fulfill our artistic visions and talk passionately about our skill, creativity and progress as artists.
Our curriculum entwines the practical, theoretical and disciplinary knowledge necessary to support a broad and rich understanding of the key aspects of art and design. Our Together value underpins our ongoing whole school (and whole stakeholder) art projects.
Art at Shipton Bellinger Primary School
Keep checking back throughout the year to see photos and comments about our developing curriculum.

Curriculum Knowledge Organisers
At the beginning of each new topic, teachers prepare a knowledge organiser that is shared with the children. Each knowledge organiser provides a summary of key vocabulary, important people and visuals to support learning new information that is referred to throughout the curriculum area.
Examples of these can be found on each subject page or by selecting individual year groups below.
Get in Touch

Design and Technology
DT is taught through a structured curriculum with carefully balanced knowledge, skills and free artistic expression. Learners work carefully to a design brief, research the current products available and then show their creativity in designing and making a product that meets a clear purpose.
Our ambitious curriculum incorporates practical activities, close evaluation and thorough evaluation. Our DT learning is always purposeful with a real world context.
Design and Technology at Shipton Bellinger Primary School
Keep checking back throughout the year to see photos and comments about our developing curriculum.
Get in Touch

English
Welcome to the English page of our school website. This is the place to come to find out more information about how we teach your child to read, write and communicate effectively. We pride ourselves in setting high standards in all aspects of the English curriculum. Children are encouraged to develop their creativity and imagination through a regular diet of: speaking and listening; focused reading; and inspired writing sessions.
Reading and writing are at the heart of the school day. The majority of our written work is cross-curricular and teachers create meaningful links between topics to ensure writing lessons are engaging. Emphasis is placed on using high quality literature as a stimulus for writing and teachers consider the importance of finding meaningful purposes for writing that inspire the children.All the National Curriculum objectives are covered thoroughly in a creative way that seamlessly links text, sentence and word level activities.
On this page, you will be able to find curriculum information, helpful links, homework support and our English policies. This information is just a snapshot of our English provision - please get in contact if you would like any additional information about English at Shipton. We believe passionately that true literacy is the ability to gain, utilise and communicate with powerful knowledge. This knowledge is our children’s key to the brightest and best future. Enjoyment of and engagement with English begins with a vibrant talk-based curriculum in the earliest days of EYFS and, through structured, sequential, rigorous teaching, it is carried with our Year 6 leavers through the rest of their lives.
As always, please get in contact with us if you have any questions or would like more information about your child's English journey here at Shipton Bellinger.
Speaking and Listening
Throughout their time at Shipton Bellinger Primary Shool, children develop as confident spearkers and focussed listeners. From EYFS onwards, children are taught how to speak for different purposes. They perform in assemblies in front of the whole school; 'in role' as historical characters: interview numerous adults; debate their point of view on a variety of topics; read plays aloud; and present informative reports to their peers.
Our intention is for children to:
Approaches to teaching and learning encourage pupils to voice their ideas in small group and class discussions, as we recognise that sharing and explaining concepts with peers enhances learning. Staff model the use of higher level vocabulary within their speech and expanding children’s vocabulary is a key focus from EYFS onwards. Subject specific vocabulary is embedded across the curriculum, through teacher modelling, in context. Contextual learning helps children to understand new words and supports them in including them in their work.
Guided Reading sessions encourage pupils to explore unfamiliar vocabulary and expand their knowledge of words. Staff model correct grammar in speech and encourage children to reflect this in their use of spoken and written language. Children are given the chance to orally rehearse ideas for writing regularly.
Drama is used across the curriculum to explore and engage children in their learning. This gives children the chance to embed vocabulary in shared activities.
By the time they leaev us at Year 6, all pupils have the confidence and necessary skills to perform in a production, which grows year on year in quality and profressionalism.
Reading
We want children to develop a passion for reading that will last a lifetime. Children are encouraged to read for pleasure and to read across the curriculum to support their knowledge and understanding in all core and foundation subjects. Reading lessons are taught consistently as part of the weekly teaching and learning sequence of English lessons so that children are taught the skills necessary for interrogating texts. We also allocate daily time to teach reading across the school in age and stage appropriate ways.
Did you know that just 10 minutes of reading a day exposes readers to over one million new words per year? It adds up to over 60 hours of reading annually, and hugely supports cognitive development and imagination whilst boosting empathy skills and reducing stress. It’s win win!
Your child’s teacher can advise on specific reading strategies and targets for your child, but you can support reading at home with these simple steps:
Listen to your child read - let them sound out the tricky words!
Please see the files at the bottom of this page for more useful information on how you can support and inspire reading at home, as well as some examples of how we celebrate and foster enjoyment of reading at Shipton Bellinger.
Little Wandle Scheme for Phonics and Reading
We use Little Wandle Letters and Sounds as our systematic, synthetic phonics scheme at Shipton Bellinger Primary School. Discrete phonics teaching is taught in the earliest days of Early Years and continues until our learners have a mastery of the graphemes and phonemes that make up the English language and are able to apply them to read a wide range of words fluently. We follow the scheme of sessions to deliver high quality sessions daily in Early Yeras and Year 1 before transitioning to Bridge to Spelling in Year 2. Children who have not mastered the sounds required at key milestones receive additional support through Daily Catch-Up and Keep-Up sessions. Should a child need support above and beyond this, we implement our SEND programme using Little Wandle resources.
Alongisde the Little Wandle Phonics, we use the Reading Programme to underpin our curriculum and secure strong foundations in early reading. Learners take part in daily small group reading that are guided by half-termly assessments to ensure children are accessing texts appropriate to their phonics ability. They are able to access a wide range of text genres through our Big Cat reading scheme. Catch up programs are built into the Little Wandle progression to ensure that no one misses out on any of this vital knowledge. We promote reading for pleasure by enabling children to select a book following their own interests alongside a teacher selected text to meet their developing skills.
Following after the Phase Reading books, children are introduced to the Reading Fluency scheme where they can develop prosody and comprehension using a similar strucutre. Our fluency texts enable children across the school, through Key Stage One and Key Stage Two, to master the life-long skill of reading. Regular assessments continue to drive devisions made by class teachers, ensuring children have secured prior knowledge in order to build a love for reading. In Upper Key Stage Two, fluency texts sit alongside a whole class reading texts where children are supported through carefully crafted interventions.
Here is a link to our Phonics and Reading Presentation
The links below enable you to find more information about the resources used at Shipton Bellinger Primary School:

Wider Reading at Shipton Bellinger Primary School
At Shipton Bellinger Primary, reading and books are at the heart of our curriculum. Our termly topics are scaffolded by a wide variety of cross-curricular rich texts and reading is embedded throughout every subject. Through access to a wide variety of carefully curated texts and an exciting, child-led curriculum, children gain first the phonic knowledge, then the comprehension skills to read and understand anything they choose.
Whole class reading is introduced towards the end of Year 2, preparing children for our Key Stage Two curriculum. Texts are selected based on their rich vocabulary, imaginative stories and links to wider learning. A selection of fiction, non-fiction and poetry enrich the learning taking place in the classroom and support children to make connections within their own writing. Authors are selected carefully so that children are exposed to classic, heritage text alongside modern greats that deepen the links they can make in language and action.
Some of our favourite reads include:
Our vibrant school reference library, in-class reading corners and our wide range of carefully chosen reading scheme texts means that our school is full to the brim with engaging, carefully curated books!

Writing
Our English units are offered to all pupils within each year group and are designed to meet the variety of need. Learning journeys are linked to a high quality stimulus such as a text, image or video. This may not be revealed immediately within a unit, to allow children opportunities to explore, predict, investigate and reason. All units hinge on an overarching enquiry question that provides scope for child-led analysis and deeper thinking, into which appropriate National Curriculum objectives (i.e. spelling, grammar, punctuation) are weaved.
Through structured teaching of spelling, grammar and handwriting and supported by strategies such as colourful semantics, we provide the children with the tools they need to make informed writing choices. Carefully chosen model texts and text type "toolkits" mean that our learners are able to craft texts across a wide range of genres and for a wide range of real-world purposeful contexts. Writing and Reading are intrinsically linked here at Shipton and our exciting core texts provide a stimulus for writing, drama and purposeful play.
Three part learning journeys ensure that opportunities for playful exploration and cross-curricular inspiration are balanced with careful studies of relevant grammar. These build to a wide range of regular opportunities to write independently with peer and adult-supported editing to ensure the absolute best quality writing outcomes.
Additional resources can be found here:
Further Help for Parents
Grammar glossary of terms
Spelling
We recognise that spelling is an area for development at Shipton Bellinger and have introduced new strategies to improve the fluency at which children spell in independent work. Effective teaching of spelling is fundamental to ensure children build appropriate skills to be life-long writers.
Spelling is part of our Key Stage One phonics journey with time dedicated to rehearsing letter strings, grapheme/phoneme correspondence and common exception words. The Little Wandle Bridge to Spelling supports the children to make connections between their phonetic knowledge and how this impacts spelling strategies.
The launch of Spelling Shed in Key Stage Two ensures all children continue to have access to age appropriate, and developmentally appropriate, words to build their competency at spelling. They recognise word patterns, letter strings and rules behind language formation to apply in their own writing. Through fun, engaging activieties they practise, rehearse and overlearn key words, including those that are common exceptions and statutory word lists, they broaden the language available to them.
Teachers deliver daily sessions using a range of resources outlined within the scheme so that children secure core spelling knowledge.
World Book Day
Get in Touch

Geography
Geography forms part of the wider curriculum and is an enquiry led subject. We believe it is vital that children are equipped with the tools to question the world around them and discover answers to their own curiosities. We aim to ensure that all children at Shipton Bellinger Primary School develop a genuine love for geography through local field trips and engaging lessons. We promote curiosity and fascination about the world. Children are motivated to gather information using observations and geographical questioning. Children will consider their impact on the local environment and how this can have a continued global impact. They think about whether these are human or physical. We aim to instil in our children that geography equips them with knowledge about diverse places, people and the natural world. Our learners will develop a contextual knowledge of the location of globally significant places, including their physical and human characteristics.
Get in Touch

History
As Historians at Shipton Bellinger, we are always asking questions about the past. We believe that understanding our shared history helps us to understand ourselves. Our curriculum maps out the substantive knowledge that our learners need to acquire in order fulfil and exceed the national curriculum requirements. The disciplinary knowledge that is threaded through our curriculum ensures that we are developing the ability to think, evaluate, and hypothesize like historians.
Historians at our school will order, evaluate and explore the events and civilisations that have impacted on our society from the very beginnings of time right up to present day. Enquiry questions anchor our learning journeys and key concepts ensure that learners can make close, chronological links in their learning in order to revisit and reapply their historical knowledge.
We are so lucky here at Shipton Bellinger to be surrounded by fascinating local history - from Stonehenge and Old Sarum Castle to the secret Spitfire workshops on Salisbury Plain. Our curriculum inspires us to find out more about the past, our local area and ourselves!
At Shipton Bellinger we consider: who are our heroes of history?
We think carefully about how different historical figures acted, the impact they have had and the challenges they faced within their own time periods. Key Stage 2 also considered how we know about each hero by evaluating sources and considering their accuracy.
During a previous, Heroes in History hook week, each class was also lucky enough to take part in a VR Headset workshop called The Trials And Triumph of Black History. Each workshop was carefully tailored to each year group and meant that we had a unique opportunity to find out more about some different historical heroes.
Year 6 - Ella Fitzgerald
Year 2 - Louis Braille
Year 3 and Year 1 - Mary Anning
Year 5 - Katherine Johnson
Get in Touch

Maths
Welcome to the Maths page of our school website. This is the place to come and find out more information about how we teach your child maths skills and knowledge.
You will be able to find curriculum information, helpful links, homework support and our Maths policies.
We believe passionately that all children can be successful in maths and by following small steps in learning it is accessible to all. We have adopted a Mastery Approach and have adopted the White Rose Scheme to guide our practice. Children use hands-on resources to support their learning alongside visual representations, for example number lines or the part-port-whole model.
In Maths, we follow a spiral curriculum format using guidance from the Hampshire Maths Team, supplemented by other resources such as White Rose reasoning. Our lessons and units of work are structured to give children a deep understanding of mathematical concepts and this allows them to build their confidence and competence in Maths. By working through a vast range of fluency, reasoning and problem solving activities, children become independent, reflective thinkers with skills that support them across the curriculum.
As always, please get in contact with us if you have any questions or would like more information about your child's maths journey here at Shipton Bellinger.
Teaching for Mastery
For children to be successful in maths reasoning and problem solving, fluency in maths is essential. Children should be able to count and recall key number facts in line with age-related expectations. Therefore every maths lesson begins with recalling key knowledge as well as embedding skills through homework.
Our units of work are designed to support a mastery approach to teaching and learning and have been designed to support the aims and objectives of the National Curriculum.
Mastering Number sessions in Key Stage One occur daily using the Rekenrek and wider counting resources. Children develop a deep understanding of the 'ness' of number and can visualise numerals in all different ways, shapes and forms. They develop early skills of subitising and the parts within a number that can be applied throughout their mathematical journey; in Key Stage Two and beyond.
In Key Stage Two, we dedicate thirty minutes each week to the overlearning and securing of multplication facts. This ensures children not only learn their times tables but understand how the relationships between them underpin much of their learning. They develop strategies to calculate problems and understand how numbers build in complexity. Multiplication Mondays is about effective teaching of times tables, not just chanting them.
All children from Year 1 to Year 6 have subscriptions to Times Table Rockstars or Numbots. These are excellent resources for practising fluency skills, such as times tables, and embedding new maths learning in class.
Concrete, Pictorial, Abstract
We believe that all children, when introduced to a new concept, should have the opportunity to build competency by taking this approach.
Progression in Calcultion
For children to grow their mathematical skills, learning must build. We use the Hampshire resources to ensure children learn calculation skills that are sequential and appropriate for their age and stage. In sharing best practise, we recognise the stages between each strategy so that children have opportunity to apply each method across their time at Shipton Bellinger Primary School.
Progression in Addition and Subtraction
Progression in Multiplication and Division.
Maths Workshop for Parents
Get in Touch

Physical Education at Shipton Bellinger is more than just sports. We believe that "the traditions and cultural reference points associated with sport and physical activity are part of our shared heritage." Our curriculum is built on the understanding that those children who develop competence to excel in a broad range of physical activities, are physically active for sustained periods of time and engage in competitive sports will lead healthy, active lives.
Being part of a community and team underpins our PE curriculum. Through our work with other schools and teams, we build strong community links and are able to demonstrate our skills in a wide variety of contexts.
Our staff receive high quality PE coaching to ensure that the quality of teaching and learning is sharply focussed with high expectations. We celebrate and are inspired by skilled sports people throughout the year when exploring global sporting events.
PE at Shipton Bellinger Primary School
Keep checking back throughout the year to see photos and comments about our developing curriculum.
Get in Touch
